planned_outcome: Land HMS Tireless: extend Zurcher inverse to free k (thermal conductivity) and c (specific heat) in addition to x_core j_0 T_oven_eff. 5-param fit with rho pinned at 1000 kg/m^3 (most product-stable). Test whether per-product physics calibration drops main-bake RMSE below the M9 Stefan baseline.
actual_outcome: 5-param Zurcher inverse (k, c free; rho pinned) implemented and tested. Synthetic recovery passes cleanly: RMSE 0.5 deg C, k within 30 percent on 20 of 20 runs. Real-CSV: 7/7 converge but main-bake RMSE 13-22 deg C (down from M11's 35-38 but still 2-4x M9 Stefan), all 7 fixtures hit j_0 lower bound, 4/7 have correlation rank-deficient. Lid bakes did find sub-cavity T_oven_eff (350K) — the radiative-BC mechanism does work as intended. Verdict CONFIRM-information-limit: even 5 free parameters cannot recover x_core well when in-dough sensors are saturated near 100 deg C. Method 4 (loaf-thickness metadata) is the only remaining path.
success_metric_result: 23 fast tests pass; synthetic recovery clean; real-CSV main-bake RMSE >6 deg C on 7/7; correlation matrix degenerate on 4/7; lag-1 autocorr 0.998 unchanged; 0/7 fixtures with all params in literature ranges.

adopt: Multi-init synthetic recovery (4 inits x 5 seeds = 20 runs) is a robust identifiability check — single-init synthetic recovery would have given misleading optimism
avoid: Treating clean synthetic recovery as evidence the inverse will work on real data — even Zurcher-class synthetic recovery says nothing about whether the data carries enough information to constrain the model
